question: When is simultaneous raw SGD with shared pooled/private own gradients a strict first-order pooled-loss descent direction?
criterion: A=||grad_W L_pool||^2+<grad_phi L_pool,grad_phi L_own>; strict descent iff A>0, ascent iff A<0; A=0 unresolved at first order.
single_binary_example: Private own gradient is a positive scalar multiple of pooled gradient under any differentiable private parameterization at finite logits.
raw_logit_geometry: Same-target CE residuals align coordinatewise for finite multiclass logits; this does not imply parameter-space alignment.
multi_example_geometry: Example-dependent positive residual weights act on tied private Jacobians; negative cross-example Jacobian products can reverse aggregate alignment.
single_multiclass_parameter_geometry: A positive-semidefinite Jacobian Gram matrix can give a negative bilinear product between distinct pooled/member residuals.
exact_witness: M4, two hypothetical binary examples, scalar shared/private parameters, all blocks active; pooled CE strictly increases along every positive SGD step on specified affine ray while all member own CEs decrease to first order.
native_optimizer_limit: AdamW moments, adaptive scaling, decay and finite OneCycle step replace the SGD field with an actual displacement requiring its own loss-direction inner product.
